content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"Every material assertion printed in the BOOK ENTRY maps directly onto a printed scripture. The core identification — butter as the word worked (churned) from milk into solid, tested doctrine that yields discernment — is carried by Proverbs 30:33 (the explicit mechanics: churning milk brings forth butter) combined with Isaiah 7:15, which in the supplied KJV text explicitly makes the butter-and-honey diet the means by which the child comes 'to know to refuse the evil, and choose the good.' The entry's clause 'teaching tested until one can refuse evil and choose good' is nearly a quotation of Isaiah 7:15. The second assertion, that butter worked into the walk cleanses the feet, is directly stated in Job 29:6 ('when I washed my steps with butter'), with John 13:5-10 supplying the register that foot-washing is cleansing of the walk of one already washed. The third assertion, that the counterfeit is smooth speech concealing war, is stated verbatim in Psalm 55:21 ('words smoother than butter, but war was in his heart'). The strongest counter-reading — butter as literal pastoral abundance/divine provision — explains 2 Samuel 17:29 and Isaiah 7:22 adequately, but it must treat Isaiah 7:15's purposive clause as merely temporal, treat Job 29:6's bizarre image of washing steps with butter as bare hyperbole, and sever Psalm 55:21 into an unrelated figure. The book's reading unifies all seven printed texts under one mechanic (working milk into a solid) and one function (discernment), including the counterfeit, and even situates Psalm 55:21 and 2 Samuel 17:29 in the same Absalom crisis. The counter offers no printed text the book's core cannot explain; the book's core explains the purposive clause of Isaiah 7:15 and the churning mechanics of Proverbs 30:33 better than the counter. By inference to the best explanation among the actual alternatives, the entry stands.","book_core_identification":"Butter symbolizes the word/teaching worked from milk (the received word) into solid, tested doctrine that produces sound judgment — the discernment to refuse evil and choose good.","book_secondary_elaborations":["Butter applied to the walk cleanses the feet (Job 29:6 with John 13:5-10 as the foot-washing/cleansed-walk register).","Butter has a counterfeit: speech worked smooth to imitate sound doctrine while concealing war (Psalm 55:21)."],"unsupported_glossary_assertions":[],"chapter_only_objections":["The chapter's reading of Job 29:6's second clause (rock = covenant, oil = pressed and proven works) is an additional symbolic stack not asserted in the entry and not independently established here.","The claim that Jael's water-milk-butter escalation runs the symbol's 'whole ladder' (Judges 5:25) is speculative and the chapter itself leaves part of it open.","The assertion that 2 Samuel 17:29's provision to David is symbolic rather than literal famine relief is an application beyond what the entry asserts.","The linkage of Isaiah 7:15 discernment to Hebrews 5:14 strong-meat discernment depends on a derivation footnoted to the Introduction and not printed with the entry."],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"Butter/curds is a literal rich dairy food functioning as an emblem of pastoral abundance, prosperity, and divine provision (Deut 32:14; Job 29:6 as prosperity hyperbole; 2 Sam 17:29; Isa 7:22 as either plenty or post-devastation subsistence), while Psalm 55:21's 'smoother than butter' is an independent physical-smoothness simile for flattery, and Isaiah 7:15's clause is temporal ('by the time he knows to refuse evil'), marking the child's age rather than a diet that produces discernment.","counter_core_identification":"Butter = material abundance and God's providential richness of the land; a concrete foodstuff, not a word-symbol.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"CONTRADICTS","material_core_denial":"The counter denies that butter carries any doctrinal referent: it holds that butter signifies material provision only, so the same referent cannot simultaneously be 'the word worked into tested teaching.' The two cores assign incompatible referents (physical prosperity vs. worked doctrine) to the same symbol.","counter_case":["Butter appears in straightforwardly literal provision lists (2 Sam 17:29; Deut 32:14; Gen 18:8), where a food reading requires no symbolic machinery.","Isaiah 7:21-22 grounds the butter in literal 'abundance of milk' from surviving livestock, fitting an abundance-or-subsistence economic reading.","Isaiah 7:15's clause is widely read temporally in modern translation, removing the diet-produces-discernment link.","Job 29:6 sits in a catalogue of prosperity images and reads naturally as hyperbole for overflowing wealth.","Psalm 55:21 needs only the physical smoothness of butter; no doctrinal register is required.","This reading matches the broad consensus of Responses A-D that abundance/provision is the most recognized association."],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Proverbs 30:33 supplies an explicit derivation mechanic — milk worked by labor becomes butter — which the abundance reading leaves as an inert proverb; given the widely attested milk-as-word figure (1 Pet 2:2), the churn yields a coherent symbol.","The supplied KJV of Isaiah 7:15 states a purposive connection ('that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good'); the book's core explains why eating butter produces discernment, while the counter must reinterpret the clause temporally against the printed text.","Job 29:6's image of washing one's steps with butter is directly explained (worked word cleansing the walk), reinforced by the printed John 13:5-10 register of foot-washing as cleansing one already clean; the counter can only call it hyperbole.","Psalm 55:21 is integrated rather than severed: counterfeit butter (smooth speech) priced against true butter, in the same Absalom crisis as the true butter of 2 Samuel 17:29 — a cross-text relationship the counter cannot use.","One core meaning accounts for all seven printed references, including both the positive and counterfeit uses, with fewer disconnected senses than the common interpretation's four-to-five independent meanings."],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["Handles the plainly literal provision contexts (2 Sam 17:29; Gen 18:8; Deut 32:14) with zero symbolic overhead.","Aligns with Isaiah 7:22's explicit causal grounding in literal milk abundance.","Matches the dominant reading in the interpretive tradition as reflected in all four common-interpretation responses.","Does not depend on the extra-entry premise that milk = the word."],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Isaiah 7:15 (KJV purposive clause tying butter-and-honey diet to knowing to refuse evil and choose good)","Proverbs 30:33 (explicit churning mechanic: milk worked yields butter)","Psalm 55:21 (explicit counterfeit: smoother than butter, war in heart)","Job 29:6 with John 13:5-10 (washing steps with butter; foot-washing as cleansing the walk)"],"unresolved_objections":["The core depends on the milk-as-word equation, which is well attested in Scripture (1 Pet 2:2; Heb 5:12-13) and in the book's method but is not among the verses printed with this entry.","Isaiah 7:15's grammar is genuinely contested; modern renderings ('by the time he knows') would weaken the purposive link, though the supplied KJV text supports the entry.","2 Samuel 17:29 and Isaiah 7:22 remain fully explicable as literal provision, so the symbolic reading is additive rather than compelled in those texts."],"confidence":"medium"}
